narrative.h2: Watercolor on screen requires keeping the paper visible

sections.heading: What watercolor actually looks like
sections.body: Real watercolor has three signatures: visible paper texture under the wash, hard-edge color pooling where pigment dried at the boundary, and the soft bleed of wet-on-wet where colors meet while still damp. AI watercolor fails when it smooths these into a generic painted look - same with motion: real watercolor frames don't tween smoothly, they boil between hand-painted cels at 12fps. The Loving Vincent film proved how powerful this looks when committed to fully.

sections.heading: Where the look comes from
sections.body: Reference canon: Loving Vincent for full-paint animation, the Studio Ghibli watercolor backgrounds (Kazuo Oga's work specifically), J.M.W. Turner's seascapes for atmospheric wash, Hayao Miyazaki's own concept-art watercolors. Children's-book illustrators: Quentin Blake's loose ink-and-wash, Maurice Sendak's cross-hatched paint. Music-video adjacent: the Glen Keane / Disney hand-drawn era, Cartoon Saloon's Secret of Kells. Tunee's watercolor model trains on real paper texture and boil animation, not digital paint filters.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Always include paper texture in the prompt: 'cold-press watercolor paper visible through wash, hard-edge pigment pooling, wet-on-wet bleed at color borders'. Specify the boil rate: 'hand-painted boil, 12fps frame replacement, not smooth tween'. Pick a palette of three to five colors max - real watercolor is constrained by what's wet on the palette. Reference one painter: 'Turner sky wash' or 'Kazuo Oga forest background' steers the model precisely.
